dedupe_keys.name: wildfire contamination of drinking water infrastructure benzene and other organics after the 2018 camp fire paradise california

description: After the November 2018 Camp Fire burned Paradise and Magalia and destroyed nearly 14,000 homes, leaving about 1,700 standing, utility tests found benzene and other volatile organic compounds in parts of the public water distribution systems. A study by state public health and water board scientists characterised the organic chemicals in a highly contaminated service line, identifying or tentatively identifying 95 compounds, 32 tied to PVC pyrolysis, 28 to polyethylene pyrolysis and 55 to uncontrolled burning of biomass and waste, and ran laboratory burns of PVC, PEX and HDPE pipe; a Public Health Institute study sampled household taps. Findings support two pathways, thermal damage to plastic pipes and intrusion of smoke, with residual chlorine changing what is seen. Coverage: one wildfire's distribution systems, with a single service line characterised in depth. Access: a free open manuscript and a project page; the licence is not stated. Caveats: one service line and lab burns, so levels elsewhere differ. It supports wildfire hazard exposure and post-fire water system recovery planning, and relates to the water utilities wildfire vulnerability data and the Camp Fire notification case study in the catalogue.
